exercises.title: Countdown
exercises.desc: Write a recursive procedure CountDown(n) that outputs n, n-1 … 1, then "Go!". Call it with 5.

exercises.title: Sum 1 to N
exercises.desc: Write a recursive function SumTo(n) returning 1+2+…+n. Output SumTo(10).

exercises.title: Power
exercises.desc: Write a recursive function Power(base, exp) — no ^ operator allowed. Output Power(2, 8).

exercises.title: Count Digits
exercises.desc: Write a recursive function Digits(n) returning how many digits n has. Output Digits(52407).

exercises.title: Reverse a String
exercises.desc: Write a recursive function Rev(s) that reverses a string. Output Rev("PAPER").

exercises.title: Linear Search
exercises.desc: Search [8,3,9,42,7,15,6] for 42. Output "Found at <index>" (1-based) and "Comparisons: <n>".

exercises.title: Minimum + Index
exercises.desc: Find the smallest value in [14,7,22,3,19] AND its position. Output "Min 3 at 4".

exercises.title: Binary Search Trail
exercises.desc: Binary search [3,8,12,17,23,31,40] for 31 — output every mid VALUE you inspect, then "Found at <index>".

exercises.title: Selection Sort
exercises.desc: Sort [9,4,8,1,6] with selection sort (find min of the unsorted part, swap it to the front). Output the sorted values on one line, space-separated.
exercises.starter:
// Selection sort
DECLARE a : ARRAY[1:5] OF INTEGER
DECLARE i, j, minIdx, temp : INTEGER
DECLARE line : STRING
a[1] ← 9; a[2] ← 4; a[3] ← 8; a[4] ← 1; a[5] ← 6

// TODO: FOR i ← 1 TO 4 — find minIdx in a[i..5], swap a[i] ↔ a[minIdx]

line ← NUM_TO_STR(a[1])
FOR i ← 2 TO 5
   line ← line & " " & NUM_TO_STR(a[i])
NEXT i
OUTPUT line

exercises.title: Stack Reverse
exercises.desc: Push each character of "STACK" onto a stack, then pop everything into one string. Output the result.

exercises.title: Ticket Queue
exercises.desc: Queue A,B,C,D,E. Serve (dequeue + output) two customers, then F joins. Output "Front: <v>" and "Rear: <v>".

exercises.title: Caesar Decode
exercises.desc: Decrypt "KHOOR" (Caesar cipher, shift 3) using an alphabet lookup. Output "HELLO".

exercises.desc: Compress "AAABBCDDDD" with run-length encoding. Output "A3B2C1D4".

exercises.title: Q1 — Array Processing
exercises.desc:
Q1 (9618/41 M/J 2021 adapted — 8 marks)
Temperatures for 8 days are stored in temps[1:8] = 21, 25, 19, 30, 27, 30, 18, 24. Write a program that finds the hottest day (the first day the maximum occurs) and the mean temperature.
Output exactly: Hottest: 30 at day 4 then Average: 24.25.

exercises.title: Q4 — OOP: Ticket Classes
exercises.desc:
Q4 (9618/41 M/J 2021 adapted — 12 marks)
Write, in your exam language, a class Ticket with private attributes rowNumber and price, a constructor that sets both, and a method GetPrice(). Then write a child class VIPTicket that overrides GetPrice() to add a 50% premium. Create one of each (row 5, price 20.00) and print both prices — 20.00 and 30.00.

exercises.title: Q5 — Text File Processing
exercises.desc:
Q5 (9618/41 M/J 2021 adapted — 8 marks)
Write, in your exam language, a program that opens scores.txt for reading, reads integer scores one per line until end of file, and prints the total and how many scores were read. Handle the file-not-found case with an appropriate message.

exercises.title: Q1 — Queue Simulation
exercises.desc:
Q1 (9618/42 O/N 2022 adapted — 8 marks)
A help desk queue is stored in q[1:6] with front and rear pointers. Join: Ali, Ben, Cy. Serve one (output the name), join Dee, serve one more (output the name).
Then output Front: Cy and Size: 2.

exercises.title: Q2 — Linked List Insert
exercises.desc:
Q2 (9618/42 O/N 2022 adapted — 10 marks)
A sorted linked list 5 → 12 → 19 → 26 is stored in data[1:5]/nxt[1:5] (0 = null, startPtr = 1). Insert 15 at node 5 keeping the list sorted, then traverse from startPtr.
Expected: 5 12 15 19 26.
exercises.starter:
// Q2 — sorted insert into a linked list (arrays, 0 = null)
DECLARE data : ARRAY[1:5] OF INTEGER
DECLARE nxt : ARRAY[1:5] OF INTEGER
DECLARE startPtr, p, newNode : INTEGER
DECLARE searching : BOOLEAN
data[1] ← 5  : nxt[1] ← 2
data[2] ← 12 : nxt[2] ← 3
data[3] ← 19 : nxt[3] ← 4
data[4] ← 26 : nxt[4] ← 0
startPtr ← 1

newNode ← 5
data[newNode] ← 15
// TODO: find the node BEFORE the insertion point, re-link newNode

DECLARE line : STRING
p ← startPtr
line ← ""
WHILE p <> 0 DO
   IF line = "" THEN
      line ← NUM_TO_STR(data[p])
   ELSE
      line ← line & " " & NUM_TO_STR(data[p])
   ENDIF
   p ← nxt[p]
ENDWHILE
OUTPUT line   // expected: 5 12 15 19 26

exercises.title: Q3 — Recursive Character Count
exercises.desc:
Q3 (9618/42 O/N 2022 adapted — 6 marks)
Write a recursive function CountChar(s, ch) that counts how many times character ch appears in string s — no loops allowed.
Output CountChar("MISSISSIPPI", "S") then CountChar("BANANA", "A"). Expected: 4 then 3.

exercises.title: Q4 — OOP: Bank Accounts
exercises.desc:
Q4 (9618/42 O/N 2022 adapted — 12 marks)
Write, in your exam language, a class Account with a private balance, a constructor, and methods Deposit(amount) and GetBalance(). Write a child class SavingsAccount adding AddInterest() that increases the balance by 2.5%. Create a SavingsAccount with 1000, deposit 200, add interest, and print the balance — 1230.00.

exercises.title: Q5 — Random-Access File
exercises.desc:
Q5 (9618/42 O/N 2022 adapted — 9 marks)
Write, in your exam language, a program that stores product records (ID : INTEGER, name : STRING×20, stock : INTEGER) in a random-access file. Write a procedure that seeks directly to the record at position ID and updates its stock, without reading the whole file.
